chunks: From him, from his father, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān al-Khazzāz, from al-Faḍl ibn Ismāʿīl al-Hāshimī, from his father, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a woman who committed zinā and gave birth to a child, and she confessed before the Imam of the Muslims that she had committed zinā and that this child of hers was from zinā, so the hadd was carried out upon her. Then that child grew up until he became a man, and a man made a false accusation against him. Is the one who made the accusation against him to be flogged?

He said: “He is flogged, and he is not flogged.” I said: “How is he flogged and not flogged?” He said: “Whoever says to him, ‘O child of zinā,’ is not flogged; rather, he is given taʿzīr, and that is less than the hadd. But whoever says to him, ‘O son of the fornicatress,’ is flogged with the full hadd.” I said: “And how has this become so?” He said: “Because if he says, ‘O child of zinā,’ then he has spoken truthfully concerning him, and he is given taʿzīr only for shaming his mother a second time, after the hadd had already been carried out upon her. But if he says, ‘O son of the fornicatress,’ he is flogged with the full hadd for his false accusation against her after her manifesting repentance and after the Imam had carried out the hadd upon her.”

key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the lawful Muslim authority before whom the confession was made and who enforces the hadd
key_terms.التَّوْبَةَ: repentance openly manifested by the woman
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the fixed legal punishment prescribed in the sacred law
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: he is disciplinarily punished with a lesser penalty than the hadd

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on insulting or falsely accusing a person born from zinā in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal distinction in cases of insult and false accusation related to a person born from zinā. Calling someone “child of zinā” does not incur the full hadd here, but warrants taʿzīr, while calling him “son of the fornicatress” incurs the full hadd because it constitutes a fresh false accusation against the mother after her repentance and punishment.
